title: Tests and dogfood keep every fixture under Temp\engram per run, clean up after themselves, and prove the leak cause fixed
outcome: Tests and dogfood never litter the user's Temp: every fixture home lives under <TEMP>\engram\run-<pid>-<random>, is removed reliably once its handles close, and each gate run proves its own run subtree is empty
acceptance: Docs state the Fair Temp Usage rule for Engram, that dogfood build targets never live under the user's Temp, and that nothing historical is deleted by scripts
Each gate run audits only its own run subtree and fails on residue, with no whole-product counts and no sweeps

Every Rust and node fixture home lives under <TEMP>\engram\run-<pid>-<random> through the shared test-support constructor and helper, the directory is the last thing dropped in every fixture that owns a store, service, verbs or child process, and a removal that still fails after the bounded retry is reported with path and OS error, never swallowed
The deterministic OS error 32 open-handle regression and the field-order negative control stay in the suite (Windows-only where OS-specific)

completion.summary: Delivered shared owned Temp/engram per-run fixtures, corrected SQLite field-drop lifetime, bounded reported cleanup and run residue audits, validated launcher-root policy, failure-safe successor cleanup, and portable documentation. Recorded Windows OS32 and original-field-order negative control; all nine parent and coordinator gates passed on reviewed freeze 664cccba. Both Mediums closed; remaining retry-pause coverage Low separately filed by coordinator. Landed ede88b8 confirmed locally with clean worktree; no historical Temp data deleted. All other work remains halted.
